title: Jack up a heavy beam, set it on two stands, then reach under
instruction: The grey steel beam is too heavy to lift by hand, and the orange wrench lies under it. Get the wrench out safely, the way a mechanic works under a car. 1. Pump the blue floor jack: press its green lever pad all the way down and let it spring back up, again and again, until the beam is at least 2 cm higher than the tops of the red jack stands. 2. The red jack stands are fixed height (no adjustment). Slide each one forward by its dark-red grip block until its column is under the beam at the cyan mark on that side. 3. Turn the yellow release knob about 60 degrees counterclockwise (seen from above) so the jack lowers the beam slowly onto both stands, and let the jack's saddle drop clear of the beam. 4. Only then pull the orange wrench out from under the beam by its grip block, toward you, until all of it is clear. Never put a gripper under the beam or within 6 cm of its edges below it, and never touch the wrench, unless the beam is resting on both stands.
context: Lifting a vehicle: Harbor Freight 2.5-ton floor jack 64543 manual (2021, https://manuals.harborfreight.com/manuals/64000-64999/64543-792363645430.pdf): "Carefully position the Jack's Saddle under the vehicle manufacturer's recommended lifting point." "Set the jack stands to the same height" ... "Slowly twist the Handle counterclockwise to lower the vehicle onto the jack stands' saddles." "Never work on, under or around a load supported only by this device." Done by: Automotive Service Technicians and Mechanics (O*NET 49-3023.00).
setup: Coordinates: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y left from their midpoint, heights above the table top. Load: a grey solid-steel beam, 10 cm (x) x 40 cm (y) x 6 cm, centred at (36, 0) cm, with two dark steel end blocks (10 x 5 x 5 cm) under its ends, one rigid body of 23 kg; its underside starts 5 cm above the table. Marks on its top and near face: yellow lift point (2 cm wide) at y 0, cyan support points (3 cm wide) at y +12 and -12 cm. Jack (fixed to the table): blue painted-steel body 12 x 9 x 3 cm at (36, 0) cm under the lift point; black steel saddle 8 x 8 x 1.5 cm (0.5 kg), top 3 mm below the beam, on a chrome ram 3 cm across that shows only as the saddle rises (visual, no collision); travel 8.5 cm, 7 mm per full pump stroke, lowering at up to 12 mm/s with the release open. Pump lever (0.08 kg): dark steel bar 8 cm long (1.4 x 1 cm) pivoting at (26.5, 0) cm, 3.8 cm high, between two fixed blue steel cheeks (4.5 x 0.6 x 4.8 cm each, at y +-1.2 cm, from x 25.5 cm to the jack body), green rubber-faced pad 3 x 4 x 1.2 cm at its tip (pad top 7.9 cm high at rest, about (20, 0) cm), spring-returned, 30 degrees of stroke (5.6 N to press fully). Release knob (0.05 kg): yellow plastic, a 4.5 x 1 x 2.5 cm wing (pointing forward at 0 degrees) on a hub 2.4 cm across and 0.8 cm tall (wing top 7.9 cm high), on a fixed dark steel post (2.4 cm across, 4.5 cm tall) at (20, -7) cm; opens from 10 degrees counterclockwise, fully at 50, stops at 90. Two red steel jack stands (1.2 kg each, fixed height: top 8 cm), each a 19 x 4 x 1 cm skid, a 2.5 x 2.5 cm column with a 6 x 3.5 cm top plate, and a dark-red grip block 3 x 2 x 4 cm on the skid's near end 14 cm in front of the column; columns start at (26, +12) and (26, -12) cm, grip blocks at (12, +-12) cm. Work: an orange steel wrench (0.32 kg): a 3 x 2 x 4 cm grip block at (26.5, 6.5) cm, 4.5 cm in front of the beam's near edge, and a 9 x 1.6 x 1.2 cm bar under the beam. Friction (static/dynamic; PhysX averages the two surfaces): beam and wrench 0.6/0.5, stands 0.4/0.35, saddle, lever and knob 1.0/0.9, fixed jack body, cheeks and post 1.2/1.0, table 0.5/0.5 (PhysX default). Start: both grippers open at the ready pose. One fixed layout.
scoring: Measured from part poses at 20 Hz. Each stage counts only with the parts at rest (beam under 1 cm/s); the best stage reached is kept. 0.25: the jack holds the beam with its underside at least 5 mm above the stands' tops (the saddle within 4 mm of the underside). 0.5: both stands upright (under 5 degrees, base on the table) with their tops within 2 cm of the beam's centre line and 1.5 cm of their cyan marks, while the jack still holds the beam as at 0.25 (underside at least 5 mm above the stands' tops, saddle within 4 mm of it); stands under 1 cm/s. 0.75: the beam resting on both stands (underside within 1.5 mm of each top), the saddle at least 5 mm below it, the beam level within 2 degrees, for 0.5 s. 1.0, success, the trial ends: then every corner of the wrench at least 1 cm outside the beam's footprint and the wrench still, with the beam still on both stands, for 1 s. 0, latched for the trial: while the beam is not resting on both stands (a beam held by the jack even 2 mm above a stand is not resting on it), a gripper's tool point, a finger tip or its wrist point (9 cm back along the fingers) inside the crush zone (the beam's footprint grown by 6 cm, below its underside), or the wrench moved over 2 cm from where it was when the beam last rested on both stands (from its start before that); the beam tilted over 10 degrees, falling faster than 0.25 m/s or pushed over 3 cm sideways; or a non-finite state.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Open the release fully so the saddle is at the bottom, then close the knob (0 degrees, wing pointing forward); set the beam on its end blocks; slide the stands back 10 cm; put the wrench back under the beam.
fidelity: Rigid primitive parts, nominal masses, friction 0.4 to 1.2 (setup). The jack's hydraulics are a stiff position drive on the saddle's prismatic joint: each full lever stroke adds 7 mm, and the open release lowers it at up to 12 mm/s. Lever (spring-returned) and knob (damped) are native revolute joints. The beam rides on the saddle and the stands by contact only. The jack is fixed under the lift point; the stands are fixed height. 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control and scoring.
